meta.description: Anima 2B LoRA, automagic3 variant of the background profile. EFFECTIVE BATCH 1, NOT 2 (corrected 2026-09-11): the background parent runs batch 1 + grad accumulation 2, but fused Automagic cannot accumulate, so accumulation is pinned to 1 here and this preset trains at half the parent's effective batch. On a 32GB desktop, raise batch_size to 2 to match the parent; on 16GB you cannot, so either accept effective batch 1 or set optimizer_params.fused: false and keep accumulation 2 (giving up fused's low peak VRAM). The author's own config uses effective batch 4 — see the exposure note at the end, latent + text-embed caching on, low_vram so idle components park on CPU. Leaves VRAM headroom for concurrent desktop use; expect roughly 2-3x the wall-clock of the performance preset. Author's recipe (rank 32, AdamW 2e-5, LLM adapter frozen — upstream's default). The ignore_if_contains list mirrors sd-scripts' Block-only targeting (no LoRA on AdaLN modulation/embedders/final projection) in upstream's diffusers module names. Note: the author's sigmoid_scale 1.3 timestep widening is not supported by upstream's Anima implementation; plain sigmoid timestep sampling is the closest available. Effective batch is a deliberate fork deviation: the author's recipe is accumulation 4, this ships 2, because at effective batch 4 the in-app step suggestion falls under its step floor on a small/medium dataset and gets clamped up — silently inflating real per-image exposure 2-3x past target. Rank/alpha/LR/optimizer are untouched author values; set accumulation back to 4 to reproduce the author's config exactly on a large dataset. If you swap the optimizer to an Automagic variant, this batch-1-plus-accumulation pattern will not work as-is — Automagic fuses its step into the backward pass by default, so gradient_accumulation must go back to 1 and the effective batch reached by raising batch size instead, which only works if the card has the headroom. automagic3 variant: the LR above is a launch point, not a target - the optimizer adapts one LR per param group from gradient sign consensus, so no scheduler is needed. min_lr/max_lr rail it (max_lr = this preset's own LR, so it can only adapt downward). Gradient accumulation MUST stay 1 unless you also set optimizer_params.fused=false: fused automagic steps every micro-batch and the trainer hard-errors at config parse otherwise. UNVERIFIED for this arch - automagic3 has no published per-arch data; Krea 2 is the only arch in this fork with a real measured run. Speed (2026-08-29): latents are served from RAM after the first pass (cache_latents + cache_latents_to_disk — disk-only caching re-read every latent every step), loss_sync_every 4, ui_db_poll_seconds 2. Training math unchanged. STEP TABLE (meta.step_table, 2026-10-12, machine-independent - the same table ships on every anima preset, laptop or desktop): 20 images ~1500, 30 images ~2250, 40 images ~3000, exact-count interpolation between rows, capped at 3000 steps. OPTIMIZED DATASET COUNT ~40 images: that is where the cap is reached; past it the panel keeps 3000 and the exposure gauge says the dataset is past the optimal size for this model and suggests curating down, instead of calling it undertrained. Source: the fork's Anima exposure target (75 steps/image, Anima-TrainFlow) - community Anima runs at LR 2e-5 report far more exposure (lilting.ch: 600-720 passes/image, i.e. ~12000 steps at 53 images), which does not transfer to these presets' higher LR, so the table caps at 3000. Values are steps at effective batch 1; the Step Suggestion panel divides by your effective batch (batch_size x gradient_accumulation), which is the only thing that differs between machines. Below the first row the first row's steps apply.
